words.means: Believing is entrusting the whole self to a personal ground that knows and loves me, standing on it, not merely accepting claims.
words.excludes: Faith as opinion without evidence, assent to doctrines one does not live, or a program for making the world better.
words.quote: in the last analysis believing, trusting, and loving are one

words.means: God is at once intimate Father and Pantokrator: family love and cosmic power held together; his might is revealed as crib and Cross.
words.excludes: Almighty as arbitrary force crushing resistance, or Father as a distant first cause who cannot be addressed or loved.
words.quote: calling God simultaneously “Father” and “Almighty”, the Creed has joined together a family concept and the concept of cosmic power

words.means: Creation is thought and freedom: God gives what he thinks its own independent being, so reality rests on meaning and love, not blind necessity.
words.excludes: God as craftsman shaping stubborn matter, the world as emanation or illusion, or a monistic ground that knows no freedom.
words.quote: the model from which creation must be understood is not the craftsman but the creative mind

words.means: Sonship is ontological, not biological: Jesus is from God in his very being, the eternal Word whose life is the Abba dialogue.
words.excludes: A good man adopted by God, or a physically begotten demigod of pagan myth; the virgin birth grounds no divinity.
words.quote: the Divine Sonship of which faith speaks is not a biological but an ontological fact

words.means: Jesus is Lord precisely as servant-king: his rule is being-for-others to the Cross, a love that commands by giving itself.
words.excludes: Lordship as domination, triumph, or the god-emperor's claim to absolute power over subjects.
words.quote: As king he is a servant, and as the servant of God he is king.

words.word: conceived by the power of the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary
words.means: His origin is new creation by the Spirit, not divine begetting: a sign of grace, of new birth given by God alone.
words.excludes: God as biological father of a demigod, the pagan myth of the god-begotten hero, or Mary as a second Christology.
words.quote: the conception of Jesus is new creation, not begetting by God

words.means: Faith is anchored in a datable event under a named governor: God saves in real history, not in timeless myths.
words.excludes: Christianity as timeless truths or archetypal myths easily detached from the awkward particularity of one man's execution.
words.quote: it simply accepts the fact that to save us God became man

words.means: Christ entered sheol, the dead's limbo of final loneliness and godforsakenness, so no depth of dying is beyond his reach.
words.excludes: A mythological underworld of the damned beneath the cosmos, or an embarrassing legend that demythologization should quietly delete.
words.quote: the word “hell” is only a wrong translation of sheol (in Greek, Hades)

words.means: God answered Jesus' self-giving love by holding him in life: love proved stronger than death, creating a new mode of life.
words.excludes: Resuscitation to ordinary mortal life, the soul's natural survival, or a symbol of nature's returning spring.
words.quote: It is the greater strength of love in face of death.

words.means: Christ's humanity is taken into God's very being: heaven is communion with God, the upper reach of existence, not a place.
words.excludes: A bodily flight upward into a three-story cosmos, as though God dwelt physically above the clouds.
words.quote: so that human existence can find its geometrical place, so to speak, inside God’s own being

words.word: judge the living and the dead
words.means: The judge is our crucified brother, whose test is love: whether we found him in the least of men.
words.excludes: A terrifying day of reckoning before a strange, distant God before whom the Christian can only tremble.
words.quote: the discovery of Christ in the least of men, in those who need my help

words.means: God's gift to history: the risen Lord's living presence, gathering believers into a new world, the Church's breath, not private fervor.
words.excludes: The Spirit as only the third Person of abstruse speculation, or as vague feeling, interiority, and edification.
words.quote: the power through which the risen Lord remains present in the history of the world

words.means: Catholic is wholeness: local churches stay Church only in visible unity, one in Word and Eucharist; holy is God's power sanctifying through sinful members.
words.excludes: A spotless club of saints, or 'catholic' as one denomination's brand of bureaucratic uniformity over rival bodies.
words.quote: they can only remain the Church by being open to one another

words.word: the communion of saints, the forgiveness of sins
words.means: Both are the Spirit's sacramental work: communion is the eucharistic bond of one table reaching beyond death; forgiveness is baptism and penance.
words.excludes: Communion as a club of the holy dead, forgiveness as cheap reassurance without conversion and sacramental rebirth.
words.quote: the word sanctorum (of the holy ones) does not refer to persons but means the holy gifts

words.word: the resurrection of the body, life everlasting
words.means: Not the soul's escape from the body but God awakening the whole person into the dialogue of love that outlasts death.
words.excludes: The Greek promise: an immortal soul naturally outliving the body it is glad to shed.
words.quote: not really as a supplement to a preceding and independent immortality of the soul
